title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, Templates, API Examples, and Docs Site Ops (Playbook)
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, API examples, docs site operations, and top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to ensure consistent, discoverable, and actionable documentation that reduces time-to-value for users integrating Redwood APIs and SDKs and reduces repeat support tickets.

Scope:
- SDK Guides (Python, Node, Go): authoring standards, required sections, and maintenance cadence.
- Quickstarts & Templates: bootstrapping examples and repo templates for common use cases (chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking).
- API Examples: canonical HTTP/REST, WebSocket/streaming, and SDK snippets.
- Docs Site Operating Procedures: deploy process, review flow, A/B testing of examples, and rollback.
- Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: triage list, root causes, and canonical responses.

Standards and Required Sections (all SDK guides and quickstarts):
1) Title and short description (1-2 sentences).
2) Why/When to use this SDK or pattern (1 paragraph).
3) Quickstart: copy-paste commands and a 5-10 line example that will work with default credentials/ENV.
4) Full example(s): end-to-end code for the recommended pattern.
5) Troubleshooting & common errors with canonical fixes.
6) Security notes (data handling, PII, key rotation).
7) Ownership and maintenance schedule (owner, reviewers, cadence).

Authoring Checklist (must be completed before publish):
- [ ] Contains working code that was smoke-tested in a clean environment.
- [ ] Includes environment variables and setup steps.
- [ ] Has a targeted SLO for example snippet runtime where applicable (e.g., streaming start < 500ms).
- [ ] Labeled with tags from the label taxonomy.
- [ ] Reviewed by at least one SDK owner and one DevEx reviewer.

Quickstarts & Templates (recommended catalog):
| Template name | Primary language | Use case | Repo/template location | Supported since | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| chat-quickstart | Python | Basic chat with system/user assistant | repo: templates/chat-quickstart-python | 2025-08 | includes streaming example |
| embeddings-quickstart | Node | Generate and persist embeddings | repo: templates/embeddings-node | 2025-11 | includes sqlite persistence example |
| pipeline-template | Go | Request routing + caching + fallback | repo: templates/pipeline-go | 2026-01 | demonstrates batch + cache config |

Quickstart Example (Python; minimal):

1) Prereqs:
- Python 3.10+
- REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment

2) Install:
```
pip install redwood-sdk
```

3) Minimal example (file: quickstart_chat.py):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is Redwood Inference?"}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

SDK Guides (structure and policy):
- Each language guide must have: installation, configuration, quickstart, advanced patterns, best practices, and a migration/upgrade section.
- Code snippets should be <= 50 LOC where possible and use the highest-level client abstractions.
- API compatibility: when server-side API changes require SDK updates, include a "Migration steps" subsection with code diffs and a deprecation timeline.

API Examples (canonical snippets):
- Maintain a small catalog under /examples with tests that run during CI and smoke test the published docs site.
- Examples must include: REST curl, Python SDK, Node SDK, and a streaming example where relevant.
- Example: Streaming chat (curl + SDK pseudo):
```
# curl (server-sent events)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (publish and rollback):
1) Branching: all content edits must be made on a feature branch named devex/docs/<short-desc>.
2) CI: docs-ci validates links, code snippet execution (examples), and linting. Any failing job blocks merge.
3) Reviewers: at least one DevEx reviewer plus an SDK owner for language-specific content.
4) Merge and Release: merged main triggers a preview deploy. After smoke tests, merge to release branch and promote to prod.
5) Rollback: if a post-deploy issue is detected, revert the release branch commit, re-run CI, and redeploy. Document the rollback in the release notes.

A/B Testing Examples and Deprecations:
- We may A/B test alternate quickstart variants (e.g., minimal vs opinionated) by routing 10% traffic to variant pages. Keep both under the same topic and track engagement metrics (time-on-page, copy/paste rate) in the analytics dashboard.
- Deprecation policy for examples: mark deprecated snippets clearly with the date, reason, and migration guidance. Keep deprecated code in the repo for 90 days unless security-sensitive.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (triage table):
1) 401 / invalid API key:
- Symptom: "401 Unauthorized" on first call.
- Canonical fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY is present and not wrapped in quotes; confirm token has not expired. Provide command: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_...`
2) Streaming connection disconnects:
- Symptom: intermittent SSE/WS disconnects after ~30s.
- Canonical fix: recommend enabling reconnect logic with exponential backoff, set keepalive ping every 20s, and ensure proxies (NGINX/ALB) have increased idle timeout (>= 120s).
3) High latency for short requests:
- Symptom: median p99 > 1s for short prompts.
- Canonical fix: check that the client is not using large batch sizes for low-concurrency use cases; recommend reducing batch window and enabling prefix caching. Provide sample config snippet for client batching: `batch.window_ms=10`
4) Unexpected tokenization or truncated outputs:
- Symptom: outputs cut off mid-sentence.
- Canonical fix: verify `max_tokens` and `stop` parameters, check that the model variant supports requested sequence length, and ensure the client flushes the request correctly for streaming endpoints.

Ownership, Review Cycle, and Maintenance:
- Ownership: DevEx docs team (eng-developer-experience) owns site-level standards. SDK packages own language-specific guides and CI.
- Review cadence: SDK guides must be reviewed quarterly. Quickstarts and top-issues must be reviewed monthly and after every major runtime release.
- Incident updates: If a customer-facing incident requires doc updates, tag the docs change with incident ID and notify the SRE and Support teams.

Metrics and Validation (how we measure success):
- Reduction in top-10 support ticket categories (target: 30% reduction year-over-year).
- Time-to-first-success metric: median time for a new user to run a quickstart successfully (target: < 10 minutes).
- Examples test pass rate in CI (target: 100% for published examples).

Appendix: Additional canonical snippets and troubleshooting commands
- Check network connectivity and DNS for api.redwood.ai:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/status
```
- Example Node snippet (embedding):
```
const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const vec = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rwd-embed-1', input: ['hello world'] })
console.log(vec[0].embedding.length)
```
